patches.valueJson: "昆虫义的 bee 经中古英语 bee，承自古英语 bēo（“蜜蜂”），属于日耳曼语的传承词。集体互助活动义有两种推测：Etymonline 认为可能来自对蜜蜂群体活动的比喻；Merriam-Webster 则认为可能经意为“邻人帮助”的方言 been、中古英语 bene，上溯到意为“祈求；祈祷”的古英语 bēn。字母名称 bee 另源于拉丁语 bē。"

patches.valueJson: "以上阶段只记录昆虫义。集体互助活动义的两种来源解释尚有分歧，不能当作定论；古英语 bēn 和拉丁语 bē 不属于昆虫义的传承链。把 busy bee 记作“忙碌的小蜜蜂”是助记联想，不能用来证明词源。"

sourceEvidence.text: The insect name continues Old English beo, meaning a bee, through the Germanic family. Etymonline presents the cooperative-work gathering sense as probably an analogy with the insect’s communal activity. This is a proposed explanation of the gathering word, not proof that the letter name or every similar-looking Old English form belongs to the insect’s ancestry.

sourceEvidence.text: Merriam-Webster keeps the insect, letter-name and gathering entries separate. The insect continues Old English beo. For the gathering word it suggests, tentatively, dialect been meaning neighbours’ help, through Middle English bene and Old English ben meaning prayer. This differs from Etymonline’s proposed communal-insect analogy. Preserve the uncertainty and do not insert prayer or the letter-name into the insect chain.
